newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER SHOWCASE-PEN PICTURES OF RANGERS PLAYERS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-PEN PICTURES OF RANGERS PLAYERS.

text.p: Pen pictures of the players most likely to play for Glasgow Rangers against Heart of Midlothian in a Scottish premier division match on Saturday.

Andy Goram (goalkeeper, age 32). Scotland's first choice goalkeeper with 38 caps to his name. Signed from Hibernian in June 1991 and has made 185 first team appearances for the Scottish champions. One of the few international goalkeepers below six feet (183 cm) in height, he makes up for his relative lack of stature with good positional sense between the posts.

Alex Cleland (defender, 26). Versatile defender who has carved out a niche at right-back since joining Rangers in January 1995 from Dundee United. Has made 40 first team appearances despite more than his fair share of injuries and suspensions.

Alan McClaren (defender, 25). Former Hearts player who moved to Ibrox in October 1994. Returned to the side on Tuesday night following a knee injury which has kept him sidelined since Rangers' 5-1 demolition of Hearts in last May's Scottish Cup final.
David Robertson (defender, 28). Left-back who loves to push forward down the touchline. Signed from Aberdeen in June 1991. Has 218 Rangers appearances to his credit and 14 goals.

Richard Gough (defender, 34). Elegant central defender and Rangers captain who joined from Tottenham Hotspur for 1.5 million pounds ($2.5 million) in 1987. A regular in the Scottish national side, earning 61 caps, before falling out of favour with manager Craig Brown. Dangerous going forward and rock solid in defence. Gough has announced his retirement at the end of this season.

Gordan Petric (defender, 27). Imposing Yugoslav-born defender who joined from Dundee United at the start of last season. Ice cool temperament. Could struggle to hold his place now Alan McClaren is back from injury.

Craig Moore (defender, 21). A graduate of Australia's prestigious Institute of Sport, signed for Rangers in September 1993 and has been on the fringes of the first team since then. Played for Australia's under-21s before gaining his first cap for the Socceroos two season's ago.

Trevor Steven (midfielder, 33). Talented midfielder capped 36 times for England under Bobby Robson. Part of the exciting Marseille side of the early 1990s, he joined Rangers from the French side for 2.4 million pounds ($4 million) in July 1992 and has scored 22 goals for the Scottish champions.

Paul Gascoigne (midfielder, 29). Arguably the most gifted British player of his generation, England's troubled clown continues to delight and repel in equal measure. Expressed regret earlier this year for an incident in which his wife was assaulted, and was banned from the Champions' League for kicking an opponent. That is the dark side to Gascoigne's character. The brilliant side was plain for all to see in the European championship where he sank Scotland with an inspirational goal. Joined Rangers from Lazio after an indifferent spell in Italy. Previously at Tottenham and Newcastle. Capped 38 times for England. Missed a penalty in his last match for Rangers on Tuesday night.

Joerg Albertz (midfielder, 25). Enticed to Rangers from Hamburg for four million pounds ($6.7 million) in the close season by the guarantee of Champions' League football. Capped twice for Germany. Likes to push forward and is dangerous from set-pieces.
Ian Ferguson (midfielder, 29). Joined from St Mirren in February 1988. Has made 251 first team appearances since then, scoring 39 goals in a career plagued by injury. Capped eight times for Scotland.

Ally McCoist (forward, 34). Now in his 14th season at Ibrox after joining from English club Sunderland, McCoist is Rangers' and Scotland's talismanic striker. With 319 goals from 510 appearances in all competitions he is the top scorer in Rangers' history. Became the Scottish league's record goalscorer earlier this month when he passed Gordon Wallace's mark of 264 strikes. Capped 54 times. Blessed with an engaging personality, he has recently made his media debut as a regular on Britain's top TV sports quiz.

Brian Laudrup (forward, 27). Classy forward with a neat pair of feet and a cool head. Joined from Fiorentina for 2.25 million pounds ($3.8 million) in June 1994 and has more than repaid his transfer fee. Combines well with Gascoigne in Rangers' front line. Capped 66 times for Denmark, where he played alongside elder brother Michael. 71 appearances for Rangers, 19 goals. Scored twice in Rangers' 5-1 destruction of Hearts in last season's Scottish Cup final.

Peter Van Vossen (forward, 28). Has yet to establish himself in the Rangers first-team since joining from Istanbul Spor of Turkey but has scored some vital goals after coming on from the substitutes' bench. Former Ajax player capped 18 times for the Netherlands.

Erik Bo Andersen (forward, 25). Classic tall centre-forward, has improved his technique greatly in recent years. Capped seven times for Denmark. Came to Rangers' attention after scoring 24 goals for Aalborg in 1994-95 season, helping them to the Danish championship for the first time in their 110-year history. Settled immediately alongside compatriot Brian Laudrup on arrival at Ibrox in February 1996. Scored a hat-trick in Rangers' midweek win against Kilmarnock.
